speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. To narrow down the cause of your double vision, limb weakness, and difficulty climbing stairs, have you experienced any recent issues with swallowing or breathing? REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, TSH.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your basic blood work is normal, let's focus on the muscle strength itself: does your weakness affect all four limbs equally, or is one side noticeably weaker than the other? Please also tell me if your eyes feel heavy or droopy, especially in the morning.

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is very characteristic. Given your double vision triggered by looking up or down, have you noticed any muscle weakness in your neck or back that makes holding your head up difficult?

REQUEST IMAGES: Electromyography (EMG) showing fatigability, MRI Brain and MRI Cervical Spine.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your description of worsening weakness with activity and double vision with upward/downward gaze, I suspect Myasthenia Gravis. Have you noticed any ptosis (drooping eyelids) that fluctuates throughout the day, or any difficulty swallowing food or liquids? REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR Antibodies, Anti-MuSK Antibodies.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Anti-MuSK_Antibodies: Not requested in current data
